points: Chapter 39 is the application of the instructions of chapter 28: the holy garments for Aaron the priest, the clothes of service to do service in the holy place, made of the blue, purple, and scarlet as the Lord commanded Moses.

note.label: Exodus 39: The Holy Garments and the Names of the Children of Israel

points: The breastplate carried four rows of stones, and the stones were according to the names of the children of Israel, twelve according to their names, like the engravings of a signet, every one with his name according to the twelve tribes; the shoulders of the ephod carried onyx stones graven the same way, stones for a memorial to the children of Israel.

note.label: Exodus 39: The Holy Garments and the Names of the Children of Israel

points: The pomegranates and the bells of gold went upon the hem of the robe round about; the word keeps saying round about, because the fringes go all throughout the garment, round about, not gathered only at four corners. Old depictions show Israelites with the fringes all the way around, and it would not hurt to put them all throughout, out of the fear of God.

note.label: Exodus 39: The Holy Garments and the Names of the Children of Israel

points: They made the plate of the holy crown of pure gold, written like the engravings of a signet, HOLINESS TO THE LORD, fastened on high upon the mitre with a lace of blue.
Black man, this is your heritage: our forefathers the priests wore crowns of real pure gold. It is a blessing to come back to this knowledge; they will not teach you this anywhere else.

note.label: Exodus 39: The Holy Garments and the Names of the Children of Israel

points: Thus was all the work of the tabernacle finished, and the children of Israel did according to all that the Lord commanded Moses; they brought every piece to Moses, and he looked upon all the work, and behold, they had done it as the Lord had commanded, and Moses blessed them.

It is like getting a building today and doing all the painting, sanding, nailing, and screwing, and then standing back and seeing the finished product: all praises to the Most High, we did it; then the people are blessed.
